definitions.explanation: A large biting fly that feeds on the blood of mammals. Common in rural and mountainous areas of Japan during summer.

examples.english: I was bitten by a horsefly.

examples.japanese: {川|かわ}の{近|ちか}くには{虻|あぶ}が{多|おお}いので{気|き}をつけて。
examples.english: Be careful near the river because there are a lot of horseflies.

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}の{山|やま}では{虻|あぶ}が{飛|と}び{回|まわ}っていて、{長袖|ながそで}を{着|き}ないと{何箇所|なんかしょ}も{刺|さ}されることがある。
examples.english: In the mountains during summer, horseflies buzz around, and if you don't wear long sleeves you can get bitten in multiple places.

notes:
Often written in hiragana or katakana (アブ) rather than the kanji {虻|あぶ}. Horseflies are a common nuisance in rural Japan, especially near water and livestock. Their bites are painful and can cause significant swelling.

The proverb {虻蜂取|あぶはちと}らず (literally "catching neither the horsefly nor the bee") means trying to do two things at once and failing at both — equivalent to the English "between two stools."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {虻|あぶ}に{刺|さ}される: to be bitten by a horsefly
- {虻|あぶ}が{飛|と}ぶ: a horsefly buzzes/flies
- {虻|あぶ}{除|よ}け: horsefly repellent

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {蚊|か}: mosquito — smaller, quieter, bites at night
- {蜂|はち}: bee; wasp — stings rather than bites
- {蠅|はえ}: housefly — does not bite, attracted to food and waste
